_meta.description: Document-rules config for dv_act_complaint — application u/s 12 PWDV Act, 2005 with multi-relief prayers
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. PWDV definitions (aggrieved person, domestic relationship, shared household) are non-negotiable.

title: Application under Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

fields.label: Current residential address of aggrieved person
Relationship to respondent (S.2(a) and S.2(f) PWDV)
Additional respondents (in-laws, family members — Hiral Harsora applies)

Basis of domestic relationship (S.2(f) — lived or have at any point lived together in shared household, related by consanguinity, marriage, relationship in nature of marriage, adoption, or family members of joint family)
Specific incidents — dates, nature, location, witnesses
Types of domestic violence pleaded (S.3 PWDV)
Protection orders sought u/s 18 (prohibit further violence, communication, alienation of assets)
Residence orders sought u/s 19 (right to reside, non-dispossession, alternate accommodation)
Monetary relief sought u/s 20 (maintenance, medical, loss of earnings, mortgage/rent)
Compensation sought u/s 22 (mental + physical distress and injuries)
Basis for territorial jurisdiction (S.27 PWDV — where aggrieved resides / carries on business / where respondent resides / where cause of action arose)
Service Provider / Protection Officer DIR filed (if any)

mandatory_clauses.name: Aggrieved Person Status u/s 2(a)
mandatory_clauses.description: Pleading establishing applicant is aggrieved person — woman in domestic relationship with respondent who has been subjected to act of domestic violence

mandatory_clauses.name: Domestic Relationship u/s 2(f)
mandatory_clauses.description: Two living or having at any point lived together in a shared household — related by consanguinity / marriage / nature of marriage / adoption / joint family

mandatory_clauses.name: Shared Household u/s 2(s)
mandatory_clauses.description: Place where aggrieved person lives or has lived in domestic relationship — Satish Chander Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja applies

mandatory_clauses.name: Respondent u/s 2(q)
mandatory_clauses.description: Adult male / or per Hiral P. Harsora v. Kusum Narottamdas Harsora (2016) any relative including female relatives

mandatory_clauses.name: Acts of Domestic Violence u/s 3
mandatory_clauses.description: Specific pleadings of physical / sexual / verbal / emotional / economic abuse with dates and particulars

mandatory_clauses.name: Reliefs Sought
mandatory_clauses.description: Identification of reliefs under S.18 / S.19 / S.20 / S.21 / S.22 with specifics

mandatory_clauses.name: Prayer Clause
mandatory_clauses.description: Comprehensive prayer combining all reliefs sought

verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {aggrieved_name}, aged about {aggrieved_age} years, resident of {aggrieved_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above application are true and correct to the best of my knowledge derived from personal experience, and matters of legal submission are believed true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Applicant / Aggrieved Person

promptInstructions: Draft an application under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.
Establish three statutory ingredients explicitly: (i) aggrieved person status u/s 2(a); (ii) domestic relationship u/s 2(f); (iii) shared household u/s 2(s).

Identify respondent(s) per S.2(q). Per Hiral P. Harsora v. Kusum Narottamdas Harsora (2016) 10 SCC 165, the word 'adult male' has been struck down — female relatives (mother-in-law, sister-in-law) may be respondents.
Plead specific incidents of violence with dates, places, witnesses, and nature (physical / sexual / verbal / emotional / economic abuse — S.3 and Explanations).
Cite Indra Sarma v. V.K.V. Sarma (2013) 15 SCC 755 for live-in relationship tests if applicable.

Shared household — refer to Satish Chander Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja (2021) 1 SCC 414 (overruling S.R. Batra v. Taruna Batra on this point): right to reside is not limited to households owned/rented by husband.
Identify reliefs sought clearly and separately — S.18 protection, S.19 residence, S.20 monetary, S.21 custody, S.22 compensation. Multi-relief is the strength of PWDV.

Monetary relief under S.20 — adequate, fair, reasonable, consistent with standard of living to which aggrieved person is accustomed. Include heads: maintenance, medical, loss of earnings, mortgage/rent. Cross-reference Rajnesh v. Neha for affidavit of assets.

Plead jurisdiction under S.27 — court of JMFC / Metropolitan Magistrate where aggrieved person resides, or temporarily resides, or carries on business; or where respondent resides; or where cause of action arose.
Mention DIR (Domestic Incident Report) by Protection Officer if obtained.
Seek ex-parte interim orders under S.23(2) where prima facie violence shown.
Tone: factual, compassionate but professional. Documentary evidence is critical — medical, police, photographs, financial records.
Note: PWDV proceedings are quasi-civil though before Magistrate — procedure largely under CrPC/BNSS (S.28 PWDV).

relevantActs.act: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005

sections.description: 'Aggrieved person' — woman in domestic relationship with respondent who has been subjected to act of domestic violence
'Domestic relationship' — relationship by consanguinity, marriage, relationship in nature of marriage, adoption, or family members of joint family
'Respondent' — read down per Hiral Harsora; includes female relatives
Definition of domestic violence — physical, sexual, verbal, emotional, economic abuse
Application to Magistrate for one or more reliefs
Power to grant interim and ex-parte orders
Penalty for breach of protection order

filing_checklist: Proof of domestic relationship (marriage certificate / cohabitation evidence / family relationship documents)
Proof of shared household (rent agreement / utility bills / ration card)
Medical records / discharge summaries / injury photographs
Financial records — bank statements, salary slips of respondent, applicant's lack of income
Affidavit of assets and liabilities (Rajnesh v. Neha proforma)
Children's birth certificates and school records
List of witnesses and witness affidavits
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: aggrieved_name and respondent_name must not be empty
aggrieved_relationship must be specified from S.2(a)/S.2(f) categories
types_of_violence must contain at least one S.3 category
At least ONE of reliefs_sought_protection_18 / reliefs_sought_residence_19 / reliefs_sought_monetary_20 / reliefs_sought_custody_21 / reliefs_sought_compensation_22 must be true
If reliefs_sought_compensation_22 is true, compensation_amount must be > 0
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
key_citations: Hiral P. Harsora v. Kusum Narottamdas Harsora (2016) 10 SCC 165 — 'adult male' in S.2(q) struck down; female relatives can be respondents
Indra Sarma v. V.K.V. Sarma (2013) 15 SCC 755 — tests for 'relationship in nature of marriage'
D. Velusamy v. D. Patchaiammal (2010) 10 SCC 469 — live-in relationship criteria
Satish Chander Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja (2021) 1 SCC 414 — overrules S.R. Batra v. Taruna Batra; broader shared household concept
S.R. Batra v. Taruna Batra (2007) 3 SCC 169 — earlier narrow view (now diluted)
Rajnesh v. Neha (2020) SCC OnLine SC 903 — uniform maintenance framework applies to PWDV monetary reliefs
Kunapareddy v. Kunapareddy Swarna Kumari (2016) 11 SCC 774 — amendment of DV application permissible
Krishna Bhattacharjee v. Sarathi Choudhury (2016) 2 SCC 705 — continuing offence; limitation
disclaimer: Lawie is a drafting assistant. The advocate is responsible for legal accuracy and filing.
